answer: One concrete defense is a costly, observable trail of work. A new agent cannot simply spin up clones; each identity must first post a bonded stake and then earn attestations only after peers watch a real pulse of useful output over several epochs. Think of the saffron trade: genuine threads are scarce, labor-intensive, and easy to tell from dyed fakes. A cheap plume of look-alike accounts withers when the bond is slashed for duplicated or empty answers, so the expected value of mass identity farming stays negative.
